old: Its name once simply meant 'a little cask' in the language that gave it shape.
It comes from a Late Latin diminutive, butticula, built on the word for 'cask.'
It shares an ancestor with the word botija, making the two doublets of buttis.
clues: This everyday container comes from an ancient word for a cask, so at its root its name means simply 'a little cask.'
A narrow-necked container, unlike a wide-mouthed jar, holding water, wine or soda under a cap or cork. It partly replaced the Old English word flasce for such vessels.
Castaways toss a message in one out to sea, babies drink their milk from one, and you might pop open one of champagne to celebrate.
